headline: GPT-6.2 is out, and people are split on it
summary: OpenAI dropped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, which are cheaper and faster. Gemini will now run errands for you, for free.

items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are out
actions: If you already have ChatGPT or codex: look for GPT-6.2 Sol or Astra in the model picker and give them a try (the sources don't say clearly which plans get them)
The Pro 200 plan already has Sol's ultrafast mode (a faster mode)
deep_dive: API pricing: Astra costs $8 per million input tokens, $0.40 for cached input, and $40 for output. That's 20% cheaper than GPT-6 Astra, and 60% cheaper on the cached part. Sol is priced the same as 6.1 Sol.
The benchmarks (like Agents' Last Exam, where they say it beats Claude Fable 5.2 by 5.5 points at only 5% of the cost) all come from OpenAI itself, so they need independent testing to confirm.
The official post only lists the upsides. Some people online say it works great and others complain, so your experience will vary. Try it on tasks you know well.
items.signals: HN 1292 points · 809 comments · Altman 7670 likes · Simon Willison, Theo, Swyx and Dan Shipper have all tried it
items.what: OpenAI released two new models. GPT-6.2 Astra is the flagship, built for the hardest professional work (slides, spreadsheets, documents, coding, research). GPT-6.2 Sol is the efficient everyday one, and a lot of OpenAI staff use it as their default model. OpenAI says both use fewer output tokens (the unit models use to count what they write, and what you get billed on) to finish a task.
items.meaning: Your usage limit goes further, and Astra's API got cheaper too. If you use codex, try Sol and see if it's good enough for everyday stuff.

items.title: Gemini runs errands for you, free
items.signals: Josh Woodward tweet 599 likes · only one source, not much detail
items.what: Google's Gemini can now handle small to-dos for you, for free. It runs on a new model, Gemini 4 Hydrogen. It can call local businesses for you (Google Duplex), pay at checkout with Google Pay, and you can forward emails to it to deal with. The Gemini and Google Workspace link-up got better too: it can write and send emails, edit Docs and Sheets, and add several calendar events at once.
items.meaning: It's a free helper for everyday chores. If you're in one of the six countries, give it a go, but a lot of the new stuff launches in the US first.
actions: Only for users in six countries: the US, Japan, South Korea, Canada, Australia and India
New features like phone calls, payments and forwarding emails roll out in the US first; the sources don't say where to find them or which plans include them
deep_dive: So far there's just one tweet from Josh Woodward, Google's product lead, so details are thin. Usage limits, whether you need a paid plan, and when other countries get it are all unclear.
Having an AI make calls, pay, or log into sites costs more if it messes up than a chat does. Start with small stuff and watch the payment confirmations.
